dedupe_keys.name: us county eagle i outages linked to nws vtec warnings 2015 2024

description: The University of Connecticut team publishes a county-hour archive linking customer power-outage counts from EAGLE-I with National Weather Service VTEC watches and warnings across the contiguous United States for 2015 through 2024. The own Zenodo record is open under CC BY 4.0 and lists combined outage-weather CSVs, a warning table and boundary shapefiles. A power-system modeller can use county event histories to calibrate weather-exposure or resilience scenarios, with model-pypsa as a possible network context after mapping counties to service areas. A caveat is that public utility outage maps and warning polygons do not identify the exact damaged asset or prove that a warning caused an outage. Spatial harmonization to counties can hide feeder-scale variation and provider coverage changes. Hourly counts should not be treated as every customer’s exact restoration time. I read the own repository description and manifest, but did not download the tables, reconstruct the space-time join, or test completeness against individual utility reports.
